title: Where to Buy Kenyan Food Abroad
excerpt: From sukuma wiki to Royco, here's where the diaspora finds a taste of home, plus a few online grocers worth bookmarking.

content: One of the first things most Kenyans abroad look for is a reliable source of home ingredients, things like Royco, Ketepa tea, maize flour, and the specific spices that make a dish taste right. The good news is that between dedicated online grocers, local African markets, and a bit of substitution know-how, most of it is easier to find than people expect.

ships pantry staples like Ketepa tea, Royco, and maize flour across the US, with curbside pickup available at select locations for diaspora communities near their stores. Ordering online is especially useful if you're not near a city with a large Kenyan or East African community, since it saves the drive and the guesswork of which local store might carry what you need.

is another reliable option, carrying Kenyan snacks, spices, and beauty products with fast shipping nationwide. Between the two, most staple ingredients for everyday Kenyan cooking are covered without needing a special trip, and both are worth comparing on shipping cost if you're stocking up in bulk rather than ordering small amounts often.

If you live near a larger metro area, a local African or Caribbean grocery store often carries overlapping staples like plantains, cassava flour, and spices used across East African cooking, even if it's not Kenyan-specific. These stores are also usually the best place to find fresh sukuma wiki or similar greens, which don't ship well and are best bought fresh and local rather than ordered online.

It's worth asking around in local Kenyan diaspora WhatsApp or Facebook groups too, since community members often know exactly which nearby store restocks specific items, or run informal group orders for things like fresh milk products or ingredients that are hard to find any other way.

body.text: What to Stock Up On When You Find a Good Source

content: Dry goods and shelf-stable items are the easiest to stock up on in bulk: Royco, Ketepa or other Kenyan teas, maize and millet flour, dried beans, and spice blends all keep well and are worth ordering in larger quantities to cut down on shipping costs per item. Fresh produce and dairy are the opposite, buy those locally and only in amounts you'll actually use before they spoil.

body.text: Cooking Kenyan Food With What's Available

content: When a specific ingredient isn't available even online, most Kenyan dishes tolerate reasonable substitutions, collard greens or kale can stand in for sukuma wiki, and any good all-purpose maize flour works for ugali even if it isn't a Kenyan brand. Knowing which substitutions actually hold up in a dish, versus which ones change it too much, comes with a bit of trial and error, but it means a missing ingredient rarely has to mean skipping a meal you're craving.
